introduction: On this Sunday, Sirach teaches that the greater you are, the more you should humble yourself. In the Gospel, at a dinner, Jesus tells the guests to take the lowest place, and tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that we have come to the city of the living God. Let us learn humility, and open our tables to those who cannot repay us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is a father to the orphan and a defender of the widow. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be humble, and that the poor may always have the first place at her table. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who hold positions of honor and power: that they may serve with humility. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor, the disabled and all who are excluded: that they may be welcomed and honored. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who seek recognition and status: that they may find their worth in God's love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may give generously to those who cannot repay us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you lift up the humble and welcome the poor. Free us from pride, and teach us to open our hearts and our tables to all, as your Son did. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The lowest place
reflection.body:
Sirach gives simple advice that runs against the way the world works: "The greater you are, humble yourself the more, and you will find favor before the Lord." God "is glorified by those who are lowly." Pride, he warns, is a weed that takes root and has no cure.

In the Gospel, Jesus is invited to dinner at the house of a leading Pharisee. He watches the guests scrambling for the best seats, and he tells them a parable. Do not take the place of honor, in case someone more important arrives and you are moved down in front of everyone. Instead, take the lowest place, so that the host may say, "Friend, move up higher." Then he gives the principle: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

Jesus is not giving etiquette lessons. He is describing God's Kingdom. In it, the humble are lifted up. Jesus himself took the lowest place: he emptied himself and became a servant.

Then Jesus turns to his host. When you give a dinner, do not invite only friends, family and rich neighbors who can invite you back. "But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind; and you will be blessed, because they don't have the resources to repay you." True generosity does not keep accounts. And the reward will come "in the resurrection of the righteous."

The Letter to the Hebrews reminds us of the feast we are invited to: "you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem." We are guests at God's table only by grace.

This week, look for the lowest place: let someone else go first, take the less comfortable seat, do the task no one wants. And invite someone who cannot repay you.
